column1: prodigious§Prodigious effort produced a modest and durable result.§**巨大的努力**换来一个不起眼却持久的结果。
prodigy§Being called a prodigy at ten is a burden at twenty.§十岁被称作**神童**，到二十岁就成了负担。
professional§There is a professional way to say no and it takes practice.§拒绝也有**专业的**说法，那需要练习。
profitable§The most profitable hour of the week is the one spent checking.§一周里**最有价值**的一小时是用来核对的那一小时。
profiteer§War profiteers were named in the appendix and nowhere else.§**战争暴利者**只在附录里被点名，别处没有。
profoundly§She was profoundly deaf and read every lecture from a script.§她**重度**失聪，每场讲座都靠讲稿。
profundity§Profundity and obscurity are easily confused by the reader.§读者很容易把**深刻**与晦涩混为一谈。
profusion§A profusion of footnotes hides the absence of an argument.§**大量**的脚注掩盖了论点的缺席。
progenitor§The progenitor of the breed was a single ewe in 1789.§这个品种的**始祖**是一七八九年的一只母羊。
prognosis§The prognosis for the building was poor and it stands today.§这栋楼当年的**预后**很差，如今仍然屹立。
prohibit§Nothing prohibits the practice; nothing encourages it either.§没有什么**禁止**这种做法，也没有什么鼓励它。
prohibitive§Prohibitive insurance ended amateur flying in the county.§**高得吓人**的保险费终结了本郡的业余飞行。
proliferation§The proliferation of standards is why nothing interoperates.§标准的**泛滥**正是一切都不能互通的原因。
prolific§A prolific correspondent, she wrote four letters a day.§作为**多产的**通信者，她一天写四封信。
prolong§Prolonging the discussion did not improve the decision.§把讨论**拖长**并没有让决定变好。
prominence§The prominence given to one witness distorted the report.§对某一位证人的**突出**处理扭曲了报告。
prominent§A prominent chin runs through four generations of portraits.§四代人的肖像里都有一个**突出**的下巴。
prompt§The prompt on screen asks a question nobody understands.§屏幕上的**提示**问了一个没人懂的问题。
promulgate§A doctrine promulgated in haste is repealed at leisure.§仓促**颁布**的教条，只能慢慢废除。
proof§Proof against damp was the one thing the design lacked.§**防潮**是这个设计唯一缺少的东西。
propagandist§A propagandist needs only one fact and a good rhythm.§**宣传**者只需要一个事实和一段好节奏。
propagate§Errors propagate through a citation chain in about four steps.§错误经由引用链大约四步就**传播**开来。
propel§A single oar cannot propel a boat in a straight line.§单靠一支桨无法让船笔直**前进**。
propensity§Timber has a propensity to move for about a year.§木材大约有一年时间**会持续变形**。
prophetic§Nothing is prophetic until after the fact.§任何东西都要事后才显得像**预言**。
propitiatory§A propitiatory offering was left at the shrine each spring.§每年春天都在神龛前留下一份祭品以求**平息神怒**。
propitious§This is not a propitious moment to ask for more money.§现在不是开口要更多钱的**好时机**。
proponent§Even a proponent should be able to state the strongest objection.§即便是**支持者**，也应当能说出最有力的反对意见。
propose§I propose we settle the definition before we argue about it.§我**提议**先定好定义，再来争论。
prosaic§After the prosaic opening the book becomes remarkable.§**平淡**的开头之后，这本书变得非凡起来。
prospect§They spent the summer prospecting for copper and found lead.§他们整个夏天在**勘探**铜，结果找到了铅。
prospectus§The prospectus is a legal document dressed as an invitation.§**招股说明书**是一份打扮成邀请函的法律文件。
prosperity§Prosperity is easier to describe afterwards than to notice at the time.§**繁荣**事后描述起来容易，身在其中却难以察觉。
prosperous§A prosperous street can be identified by its trees.§一条**富裕**的街道可以从它的树木认出来。
protege§A protege eventually has to disagree in public.§**门生**终究得在公开场合表示异议。
protest§Under protest, he signed and appealed the same week.§他在**抗议**之下签了字，同一周就提起了上诉。
provincial§Provincial museums hold the objects the capital did not want.§**省级**博物馆收藏着首都不要的东西。
provocation§The provocation was slight and the response was not.§**挑衅**很轻微，反应却不然。
provocative§A provocative question can be gentler than a polite one.§**挑衅**性的问题可能比礼貌的问题更温和。
provoke§Do not provoke an argument you have not prepared for.§不要**挑起**一场自己没准备好的争论。
proximity§Proximity breeds either cooperation or a boundary dispute.§**毗邻**要么孕育合作，要么引发边界纠纷。
prudence§Prudence in a first job looks like timidity and is not.§第一份工作里的**审慎**看起来像胆怯，其实不是。
prudent§The prudent course was also the slowest.§**审慎的**路线同时也是最慢的。
publicity§Publicity for the appeal was handled by two volunteers.§这次募捐的**宣传**由两名志愿者负责。
publicize§They publicized the finding before the paper was reviewed.§他们在论文评审之前就**公布**了这个发现。
puerile§The dispute became puerile and both sides withdrew.§这场争执变得**幼稚**，双方都退出了。
pugnacious§A pugnacious style wins arguments and loses readers.§**好斗的**文风赢得争论，失去读者。
punctilious§Punctilious about the small print, he missed the headline.§他对小字条款**一丝不苟**，却漏掉了大标题。
pundit§No pundit is ever asked about last year's forecast.§没有哪位**权威**会被问起去年的预测。
purify§Filtering purifies the water and removes nothing you can taste.§过滤**净化**了水，却没除掉任何你尝得出的东西。
purity§Purity of the sample matters more than the size of it.§样品的**纯度**比数量更重要。
pursue§Do not pursue a footnote past the second archive.§一条脚注**追到**第二个档案馆就该停了。
purveyor§By appointment, purveyor of tea to the household since 1832.§奉旨**供应**，自一八三二年起为该府邸供应茶叶。
quaint§Quaint is what we call a building we no longer have to live in.§我们把自己不必再住的房子称作“**古雅**”。
qualitative§A qualitative difference cannot be fixed by a bigger sample.§**质的**差别无法靠扩大样本来弥补。
quantify§Quantify what you can and describe the rest honestly.§能**量化**的就量化，其余的诚实地描述。
quarantine§New books were quarantined for a week before shelving.§新书上架前要**隔离**一周。
quarrelsome§A quarrelsome draft becomes a generous book by the third pass.§一份**好斗**的草稿到第三遍就成了一本宽厚的书。
quash§He quashed the rumor by publishing the whole ledger.§他公布了整本账簿，**平息**了谣言。
quell§A cup of tea quelled a disagreement three memos had not.§一杯茶**平息**了三份备忘录都没能平息的分歧。
querulous§A querulous tone undermines a legitimate complaint.§**抱怨**的语气会削弱一个正当的投诉。
query§Every query in the margin turned out to be worth answering.§页边的每一条**疑问**最后都值得回答。
questionable§A questionable date is better flagged than quietly corrected.§**可疑**的日期最好标出来，而不是悄悄改掉。
quibble§I have one quibble and it is about the title.§我有一点**小意见**，是关于标题的。
quicken§Her interest quickened when she saw the second signature.§看到第二个签名时，她的兴趣**立刻被点燃**。
quiescent§The disease is quiescent and monitored every six months.§病情处于**静止**期，每半年复查一次。
quixotic§A quixotic campaign changed three laws by losing.§一场**不切实际的**运动靠失败改变了三部法律。
quizzical§A quizzical eyebrow is the cheapest form of criticism.§挑起的一道**疑惑**的眉毛是最廉价的批评。
